extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational journalism researchers and developers building newsroom assistive tools
extracted.subtask_description: Predict whether public policy items (e.g., bills, meeting items, press releases) will be covered by news outlets, and link policy documents/meetings to news articles using low-annotation linking methods. Evaluation combines automatic metrics and expert journalist human evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probabilistic relational linking methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Link news articles, public policy documents and meeting recordings using probabilistic relational modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a low-annotation linking methodology that outperforms other retrieval-based baselines; recommended when labelled links are scarce. Emphasis on modeling relations across heterogeneous corpora rather than relying purely on retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and perform the task of newsworthiness prediction: to predict if a policy item will get covered by the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat newsworthiness as a binary (covered / not covered) prediction for policy items; incorporate signals from different aspects of public policy discussion because different aspects yield different newsworthiness signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metric — F1 for identifying newsworthy policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use F1 score to measure how well systems identify policies that expert journalists consider newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported human-evaluation result: systems identify policies journalists consider newsworthy with 68% F1. Use human-labelled judgments as the gold standard when computing F1 for this task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation — coverage recommendation helpfulness (win-rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure whether coverage recommendations are helpful to journalists via human evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported helpfulness in the paper as an 84% win-rate; framing evaluation as comparative/human-preference tests (win-rate) to assess practical utility of recommendations beyond automatic metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data linking across heterogeneous corpora
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and link news articles, public policy documents, and meeting recordings to form the dataset for newsworthiness analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because few labelled links exist and language use differs across corpora, prefer linking approaches that require little annotation and model cross-corpus relations explicitly; dataset should include multiple source types (articles, documents, recordings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to label scarcity, corpus heterogeneity, and multi-causal coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods must handle three main challenges: very few labelled links, differing language use between corpora, and the fact that text may be covered for a variety of reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluate systems with these constraints in mind — e.g., low-annotation approaches, domain-transfer-aware models, and analyses that account for multiple possible reasons for coverage rather than assuming a single signal.
